name: Arena Night A — Reference Fidelity Hard Gate
changeReason: Candidate B2 received a false PASS because general polish, brand recognition and usability compensated for missing high-salience properties of the user-selected A reference. Reference fidelity is now evaluated before and independently of general visual quality.

reference.comparisonRule: Compare the candidate and canonical A panel at equal phone height. Judge rendered pixels only; asset provenance, implementation rationale and build status are excluded.

nonCompensationRule: If A_REFERENCE_FIDELITY fails, the overall verdict is FAIL. General visual quality, brand recognition, official assets, technical compliance, usability, build success and platform smoke cannot raise or compensate for that verdict.

scoring.passRule: All four criteria must individually score >=4. Average, total score and strengths in another criterion cannot compensate for one criterion below floor.

criteria.label: 群像冲突
criteria.referenceInvariant: The A hero is a multi-subject confrontation, not a mascot portrait. Pikachu is the dominant foreground actor; at least one opposing character is clearly legible; additional arena/crowd silhouettes amplify a shared battle event.

scoreAnchors.0: No character event or only decorative brand objects.
scoreAnchors.1: One isolated mascot on a background.
scoreAnchors.2: A second character exists but is hidden, tiny, passive or unrelated.
scoreAnchors.3: Two characters are visible and share a setting, but confrontation/reaction is weak and the scene still reads as a portrait.
scoreAnchors.4: Primary and opposing subjects form an unmistakable confrontation; supporting arena/crowd cues reinforce the same event.
scoreAnchors.5: A rich but controlled ensemble forms one decisive battle moment, with foreground protagonist, opponent, environmental reaction and audience/arena energy.

hardFailureSignals: Pikachu remains the only immediately legible character.
Opponent is visible only after careful inspection or functions as a background watermark.
Characters share a frame but have no visible opposition, reaction or common target.
Cards, photos or UI chrome are used to simulate a group scene.

criteria.label: 电光爆发
criteria.referenceInvariant: A uses a concentrated, high-energy electrical burst around the protagonist as both action evidence and scene light. It must visibly affect nearby subjects, floor and atmosphere.

scoreAnchors.1: Small decorative spark, glow or color streak.
scoreAnchors.2: Energy is visible but disconnected from character action and does not illuminate the scene.
scoreAnchors.3: A coherent energy source exists and affects part of the scene, but lacks the explosive visual mass or focal force of A.
scoreAnchors.4: A strong electrical burst is attached to the protagonist's action and creates visible rim/cast light, particles and atmospheric response.
scoreAnchors.5: The burst becomes the organizing light/action engine of the composition, radiating through subjects, floor, effects and crowd while preserving readability.

hardFailureSignals: Lighting is primarily passive colored beams with no explosion or discharge.
Glow exists only behind/under a character and has no scene consequence.
Generic particles or gradients substitute for directional electricity.
Energy can be removed without changing the depicted action.

criteria.label: 动作方向
criteria.referenceInvariant: A's subjects, lightning, spotlight and arena diagonals converge into a forceful directional flow. The eye should enter, hit the protagonist/action and continue toward the opponent or CTA—not stop at a centered static mascot.

scoreAnchors.2: A few diagonal decorations exist but subjects remain static and disconnected.
scoreAnchors.3: The composition has a readable diagonal or forward motion, but character poses/effects do not fully support it.
scoreAnchors.4: Character pose, opponent placement, electrical trajectory and arena lines form one clear attack/counterattack direction.
scoreAnchors.5: Multiple directional vectors converge and release with poster-like control, producing immediate kinetic tension without visual confusion.

hardFailureSignals: The protagonist is upright, centered and front-facing without a force vector.
Opponent placement does not establish attack/counterattack geometry.
Background beams move independently of character poses.
Typography supplies all perceived motion while the scene itself remains static.

criteria.label: 赛事海报冲击
criteria.referenceInvariant: The first glance must feel like a premium battle-event poster: one spectacular image mass, decisive headline, extreme scale contrast, controlled darkness and a charged crowd/arena atmosphere.

scoreAnchors.0: Generic app header or content card.
scoreAnchors.1: Branded hero with logo and character but no event spectacle.
scoreAnchors.2: Promotional composition with several elements but weak focal mass and emotional escalation.
scoreAnchors.3: Competent event poster with clear headline and subject, but insufficient scale, atmosphere or dramatic climax compared with A.
scoreAnchors.4: Immediate premium event-poster impact: dominant spectacle, strong type-image lockup, controlled supporting information and arena tension.
scoreAnchors.5: Matches A's first-glance intensity and cinematic density while remaining original, readable and usable in the host.

hardFailureSignals: The hero reads primarily as an app landing page rather than an event poster.
Large dark/empty areas weaken rather than intensify the spectacle.
Headline is dramatic but the underlying image mass is passive.
Logo, labels or UI metadata are doing the emotional work that the scene should do.

generalVisualQuality.passRule: Total >=57 and every dimension meets its floor. No dimension may compensate for another floor failure.

required: GENERAL_VISUAL_QUALITY: >=57/70 and every dimension floor met
No global hard blocker from arena-a-visual-rubric.json
overallReleaseRule.visualScoreDisplay: Report A fidelity as four separate 0–5 scores and general quality separately. Do not collapse both into a single compensating percentage.

qaOutputContract.correctionRule: If reference fidelity fails, the shortest correction path must address the lowest-scoring A criterion first and may not prescribe polish, spacing or token changes as the primary fix.
qaOutputContract.independence: Each B3/C3 candidate is judged from a fresh screenshot by a QA context that did not implement it and has not received its rationale.

retroactiveFinding.reason: B2 achieved general cohesion and usability but did not meet A floors for electric burst, action direction and event-poster impact. The previous weighted model allowed unrelated strengths to compensate, creating a false PASS.
